title: How does C corporation income tax before an owner takes cash work?
description: The corporation computes its own taxable income and generally pays federal corporate income tax at 21%, with state and other applicable rules reviewed separately.

title: How does a C corporation dividend and its second tax layer work?
description: A dividend generally comes from after-tax corporate earnings and is not a corporate deduction. Shareholder dividend tax rules can add a second tax layer.

title: How does retaining earnings in a C corporation work?
description: Retaining cash leaves it inside the company for company purposes. Corporate tax can still apply to taxable profit; cash retention does not make the earnings untaxed.

title: How does owner payroll as a C corporation expense work?
description: Reasonable compensation for actual services can generally be a corporate business expense, subject to applicable rules.

title: How does a C corporation capital contribution work?
description: A shareholder investment is generally capital funding, not customer income. It belongs in the ownership and basis records rather than the sales ledger.

title: How does equipment purchases inside a C corporation work?
description: The purchase exchanges cash for an asset. A current deduction depends on depreciation rules, eligible expensing, service date and use.

title: How does a corporate loan to a shareholder work?
description: A genuine corporate loan creates shareholder debt. Repayment intent, terms, interest and actual conduct must support the loan.

title: How does a C corporation business reserve work?
description: Corporate cash should be considered in light of actual business needs and applicable accumulation rules.

title: How does a C corporation loss at the company level work?
description: A C corporation operating loss generally stays with the corporation rather than passing through as the shareholder's personal deduction.

title: How does the transition from C corporation to S taxation work?
description: An S election changes the federal framework if eligibility and procedure requirements are met, but prior C corporation history can still matter.

title: How does S corporation profit on an owner return work?
description: S corporation items pass to owners on Schedule K-1, subject to applicable limitations. Retaining corporate cash does not generally stop pass-through income.

title: How does S corporation payroll versus distributions work?
description: S corporation payroll pays for shareholder services. Distributions have separate basis rules; working shareholders must address reasonable compensation.

title: How does an S corporation stock basis increase work?
description: Allocated income generally increases stock basis, while distributions and other adjustments can reduce it.

title: How does an S corporation distribution above basis work?
description: A nondividend distribution is generally tax-free only to the extent of stock basis; an excess can create gain. Debt basis does not automatically shelter a distribution.

title: How does S corporation loss limitation review work?
description: Allocated losses must pass through stock and debt basis, at-risk, passive activity and excess business loss rules as applicable.

title: How does shareholder funding for business expenses work?
description: Owner capital or a bona fide direct loan can fund S corporation operations. Funding is not itself an expense; classify what the business buys.

title: How does S corporation health insurance reimbursement work?
description: More-than-2% shareholder premiums paid or reimbursed by the corporation have special wage and deduction treatment.

title: How does debt basis when only one shareholder lends work?
description: A genuine direct loan can create debt basis for the lending shareholder under applicable rules. Other shareholders do not automatically get the same basis.

title: How does an S corporation tax distribution work?
description: An S corporation tax distribution generally remains an owner distribution, not a corporate income-tax deduction. State entity taxes need separate review.

title: How does an S corporation shareholder loan repayment work?
description: A genuine loan repayment reduces the company debt and must be compared with the shareholder's adjusted debt basis. A distribution uses stock-basis rules.

title: How does partnership income from Form 1065 to the partner work?
description: A partnership generally allocates items on Schedule K-1. Partners report their shares under applicable rules; cash distributions need not equal allocations.

title: How does partnership profit allocation versus cash distribution work?
description: Partnership profit allocations determine taxable shares. Cash distributions affect basis and can create gain when they exceed outside basis.

title: How does a guaranteed payment to a partner work?
description: A qualifying guaranteed payment is determined without regard to partnership income. Its reporting and deduction or capitalization depend on the facts.

title: How does a partner capital contribution work?
description: Cash or property contributed as capital funds the partnership and generally affects the contributing partner's outside basis.

title: How does partnership debt in outside basis work?
description: A partner's share of qualifying liabilities can affect outside basis. Liability type and allocation matter; basis is not the same as being at risk.

title: How does partnership losses on the partner return work?
description: The partnership allocates the loss, but the partner must apply outside-basis, at-risk, passive and other applicable limitations.

title: How does a partnership tax distribution work?
description: The partnership can distribute cash under its governing agreement to fund partners' tax obligations. Taxable allocations and distribution treatment remain separate.

title: How does participation in a rental partnership work?
description: The partnership allocates economic items under applicable rules, while material participation is generally evaluated for each owner.

title: How does reimbursing a partner business expense work?
description: A reimbursement accounts for actual partnership business costs paid by a partner, while a guaranteed payment compensates under its own rules.

title: How does buying a partnership interest rather than its property work?
description: An interest purchase creates outside basis for the buyer, while the partnership owns its assets with inside basis.

title: How does the split from gross wages to net pay work?
description: Gross wages are reduced by applicable employee taxes and other authorized deductions to arrive at net pay. The employer remits withheld amounts under deposit rules.

title: How does the employer share of payroll taxes work?
description: The employer can owe payroll taxes in addition to the employee amounts withheld from wages. Rates, wage bases and special rules depend on the tax and year.

title: How does remitting payroll withholding to the IRS work?
description: Amounts withheld must be deposited and reported according to the employer's applicable schedule.

title: How does payroll for a sole S corporation shareholder work?
description: A single working shareholder still needs supported wage treatment and applicable employment-tax reporting. Reasonable compensation is based on actual services.

title: How does a bonus payment through payroll work?
description: A cash bonus generally has withholding and payroll tax treatment. Supplemental-wage withholding need not equal the employee's final income-tax rate.

title: How does an employee 401(k) payroll deferral work?
description: An eligible elected deferral is withheld from compensation and sent to the plan under applicable requirements.

title: How does employee versus contractor payment classification work?
description: The worker's actual relationship determines whether employee payroll or independent-contractor treatment applies.

title: How does employee reimbursement versus additional wages work?
description: A properly substantiated reimbursement under an accountable arrangement can be treated differently from wages. Nonaccountable payments generally need wage treatment.

title: How does paying a spouse through business payroll work?
description: A spouse must perform genuine services, and compensation and payroll treatment depend on the entity and applicable family-employment rules. Record duties and actual pay.

title: How does reconciling Form 941 and W-2 totals work?
description: Quarterly payroll reporting and annual employee reporting should connect to the payroll records, with differences investigated and corrected appropriately.

title: How does a real management fee between two entities work?
description: Management fees require actual services and a supportable arrangement. Review payer deduction or capitalization, related-party rules and recipient income.

title: How does related-party pricing in a two-entity arrangement work?
description: Controlled transactions must be supportable under applicable pricing and allocation rules.

title: How does separating property ownership from operations work?
description: Separate ownership can distinguish operating activity from property ownership, but tax classification and related-party use still matter.

title: How does shared payroll cost allocation between entities work?
description: Actual employees, services and cost allocation must be documented. Employment, benefit-plan, agency and related-employer rules need review before centralizing payroll.

title: How does a royalty between commonly owned companies work?
description: A royalty needs genuine intellectual-property rights, actual use, supportable pricing and consistent reporting. Legal ownership and development history matter.

title: How does a loan between commonly owned entities work?
description: A bona fide loan creates a payable for one entity and a receivable for the other. Principal is generally a balance-sheet movement rather than a service expense.

title: How does a parent capital contribution to a subsidiary work?
description: Equity funding increases the investment and capital records; it is not a deductible fee for services merely because money leaves the parent account.

title: How does paying a vendor from the wrong entity account work?
description: Identify which entity incurred the obligation and whether the other entity paid as an agent, lender or investor.

title: How does a transfer between two commonly owned LLCs work?
description: Tax treatment of transfers between commonly owned LLCs depends on federal classification. Disregarded entities can differ from separate taxpayers.

title: How does owner cash extraction in a two-entity plan work?
description: Follow the cash through both entities and then the owner payment. A payer deduction may create recipient income, and a corporate dividend can add shareholder tax.

title: How does rental income reporting from tenant to owner work?
description: Reconcile gross rent and other rental receipts with property expenses and depreciation, then apply applicable limitations on the owner return.

title: How does a rental mortgage principal and interest split work?
description: Principal reduces debt, while qualifying interest can be a rental expense under applicable rules.

title: How does noncash depreciation against rental income work?
description: Depreciation allocates qualifying property basis over time or under eligible acceleration rules. It can create a tax expense without a current cash payment.

title: How does depreciation after home-to-rental conversion work?
description: Establish the rental service date and apply the conversion basis rules, which can use the lower of adjusted basis or fair market value for depreciation.

title: How does a rental improvement on the asset schedule work?
description: A capital improvement is generally added to an asset schedule rather than deducted as an ordinary repair. Identify its cost, classification and service date.

title: How does rental security deposit accounting work?
description: A refundable deposit is generally tracked as a liability until returned or applied under the lease. Advance rent is different.

title: How does vacation rental personal-use allocation work?
description: Personal and rental use can require expense allocation and trigger special vacation-home limitations.

title: How does a short-term rental loss on the household return work?
description: Classify the activity, evaluate participation and apply basis, at-risk, passive and other relevant limits.

title: How does property manager fees and net remittances work?
description: The manager may collect rent, deduct fees and remit net cash, but the owner must reconcile gross income and qualifying expenses.

title: How does rental sale gain versus net closing cash work?
description: Tax gain generally uses amount realized and adjusted basis, while closing cash also reflects mortgage payoff and settlement items.

title: How does an employer retirement plan contribution work?
description: The employer funds the retirement account under the plan rules, with deduction timing, limits and employee requirements reviewed separately.

title: How does a pretax employee salary deferral work?
description: Eligible pretax salary deferrals generally reduce current federal income-tax wages, while employment-tax treatment must be applied separately.

title: How does a Roth 401(k) payroll deferral work?
description: A designated Roth deferral generally uses compensation included in current taxable income. Qualified withdrawal treatment differs from pretax money.

title: How does a cash balance plan funding obligation work?
description: A cash balance plan is a defined benefit plan with actuarial calculations and ongoing funding requirements.

title: How does retirement coverage after hiring employees work?
description: Eligible common-law employees can change an owner-only plan's participation and testing requirements.

title: How does S corporation salary for retirement contributions work?
description: Eligible compensation, generally W-2 wages, supports S corporation retirement plan calculations. Distributions do not create compensation for this purpose.

title: How does a SEP employer contribution work?
description: A SEP generally involves employer contributions under its eligibility and allocation rules; it is not the same mechanism as employee 401(k) salary deferrals.

title: How does retirement coverage across two companies work?
description: Controlled-group and affiliated-service-group rules can require businesses to be considered together.

title: How does retirement funding alongside business expansion work?
description: Funding moves cash out of business liquidity and into the plan, even when a deduction lowers current tax.

title: How does a retirement contribution correction with payroll work?
description: The correction depends on whether the problem is an excess deferral, annual addition, employer deduction or operational error.

title: How does an accountable plan reimbursement work?
description: The employee substantiates a qualifying business cost and returns excess advances; the company records the reimbursement under the applicable rules.

title: How does an owner-paid expense for the correct entity work?
description: Identify which taxpayer incurred the business obligation, then document reimbursement, contribution or another appropriate arrangement.

title: How does mixed-use vehicle expense allocation work?
description: Separate business, commuting and personal use, then apply an eligible expense method consistently. A company payment does not make all miles business-related.

title: How does the business meal deduction review work?
description: The business purpose and substantiation must support the underlying expense, and applicable deduction limits still apply.

title: How does travel advances and expense reconciliation work?
description: Substantiated qualifying costs under an accountable arrangement can receive different treatment from a nonaccountable allowance.

title: How does depreciation versus immediate expensing work?
description: Depreciation recovers qualifying asset cost under tax rules over time or eligible acceleration provisions. Expensing requires its own eligibility and election analysis.

title: How does business interest versus principal repayment work?
description: Qualifying business interest can have expense treatment, subject to limits and tracing. Principal repayment reduces debt and generally is not an expense.

title: How does an expense correction across business and personal returns work?
description: An expense adjustment can change entity income, owner allocations, basis and the household calculation.

title: How does home office eligibility before reimbursement work?
description: A home office needs eligible use and supporting records; reimbursement and individual deduction treatment depend on the owner's employment and entity facts.

title: How does preventing duplicate owner reimbursements work?
description: Document each business expense, purpose and prior payment or reimbursement. One cost should not be reimbursed or deducted twice because both owners used it.

title: How does an owner loan on the business balance sheet work?
description: A genuine advance creates a business payable and an owner receivable. Principal funding is not customer income or a wage expense.

title: How does owner equity funding versus a business loan work?
description: Capital is an ownership investment, while a genuine loan creates a repayment obligation. The economic facts and documentation determine treatment.

title: How does repayment of a loan with reduced debt basis work?
description: An S corporation loss deduction can reduce basis in qualifying shareholder debt. Loan repayment can then be taxable; reconcile any basis restoration.

title: How does a shareholder guarantee versus a direct loan work?
description: A guarantee commits the owner to possible repayment but generally does not itself create S corporation debt basis. A bona fide direct advance has different facts.

title: How does shareholder loan interest reporting work?
description: Interest is separate from principal and can create income to the lender, with payer deduction treatment subject to applicable rules.

title: How does stock basis versus company bank cash work?
description: Stock basis reflects owner investment and prescribed tax adjustments. Company cash from borrowing, earnings or other events does not establish that basis.

title: How does a stock contribution before a distribution work?
description: A genuine capital contribution generally increases stock basis, while a later distribution must be evaluated under the applicable ordering and distribution rules.

title: How does intercompany loan principal repayment work?
description: Principal repayment settles a liability; it is not generally a deductible operating expense.

title: How does classification of company-paid personal bills work?
description: Identify whether the payment is compensation, a distribution, a bona fide loan or another supported item.

title: How does a loan schedule in the business return work?
description: Opening principal, advances, repayments, interest and ending balances should reconcile with the books and supporting agreements. Tax basis can differ from principal.

title: How does estimated tax versus payroll withholding work?
description: Estimated payments are made directly toward the owner's tax liability, while payroll withholding is taken from compensation and remitted through the employer.

title: How does a tax reserve followed by an owner payment work?
description: A business tax reserve is not a deduction. Classify the transfer to the owner correctly; the estimated payment reduces tax due, not operating profit.

title: How does a tax safe harbor versus final liability work?
description: A safe harbor can protect against an underpayment penalty when its requirements are met. The final tax return still calculates actual liability from current facts.

title: How does annualized income for estimated installments work?
description: The annualized income installment method considers uneven income and deductions. It requires timely records and the applicable calculation, not simply delayed payments.

title: How does a rental sale in a new payment projection work?
description: A sale can add gain and depreciation-related amounts to the household return. Mortgage payoff affects cash, not the same tax calculation.

title: How does tax payments during a filing extension work?
description: An extension generally changes the filing timeline without automatically extending the tax payment deadline.

title: How does a prior-year overpayment applied forward work?
description: A properly elected carryforward applies an overpayment toward the next year's tax, with credit timing determined under applicable rules.

title: How does quarterly books in an owner tax projection work?
description: A reliable projection starts with reconciled business results and adds tax adjustments and household items.

title: How does spouse withholding for joint business income work?
description: On a joint return, household withholding can help cover combined tax. Review withholding, annual rules and other income before reducing estimated payments.

title: How does paying an individual final tax balance work?
description: A personal federal income-tax payment generally is not a business deduction. It settles the owner's liability after the return computation.
